args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the v2.3.1 deploy, checkout-api failed health checks in production (healthy=false, 18% error rate) in us-east, us-west, and eu-west. The SRE agent rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production, in all three regions. After the rollback the service reports healthy=true with a 0.2% error rate. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. The cause of the v2.3.1 failure still needs investigating before it is redeployed.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again.

- **Cause:** v2.3.1 was live in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with health checks failing and an error rate of 18%.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. I rolled back to it, and all three regions now run v2.3.0. A status check afterwards shows the service healthy with an error rate of 0.2%.
- **Incident:** I opened SEV2 incident INC-0001 for checkout-api, which paged on-call. It describes the failure, the rollback and the result.

The release candidate for v2.3.1 also failed health checks in staging, yet it went to production anyway. I included this in the incident. Someone should find the root cause before v2.3.1 is redeployed, and check why the staging failure didn't block the release.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
